You asked me to estimate Abu Qir's (ABUK) full-year 2026 EPS and compare it with Edita's (EFID) 2025 EPS. Here is what the evidence supports.

**ABUK FY-2026 EPS – a bounded estimate, not a point figure**
- Verified 9-month 2026 basic EPS: **8.74 EGP** (Jan–Sep 2026).
- I have no verified Q4-2026 or FY-2025 ABUK figure in the evidence, so I cannot pin down the fourth-quarter contribution. The Q3-2026 cell prints as "199" with an OCR flag (likely 1.99 EGP with a dropped decimal comma), but because it is marked AMBIGUOUS I have not used it in any calculation.
- Floor (Q4 = 0): FY-2026 EPS ≥ 8.74 EGP.
- Pro-rata annualisation (8.74 × 12/9): ≈ 11.65 EGP – a rough midpoint, not a forecast.
- Plausible band: roughly **9 – 12 EGP**, with the true figure depending on Q4 seasonality that the evidence does not let me verify.

**EFID FY-2025 EPS**
- Verified basic & diluted EPS for the year ended 31 Dec 2025: **2.18 EGP** (up from 1.09 EGP in FY-2024, roughly a doubling).

**Does ABUK beat EFID?**
Yes, unambiguously. Even ABUK's 9-month 2026 EPS of 8.74 EGP is about **4×** EFID's entire 2025 EPS of 2.18 EGP. For ABUK's full-year 2026 EPS to fall below 2.18 EGP, Q4-2026 would need to be a loss exceeding 6.56 EGP per share – an outcome with no support in the data provided. On the pro-rata estimate (≈ 11.65 EGP) the gap widens to roughly **5×**.

**Important caveats**
1. The comparison is not like-for-like: ABUK data is 9-month (Jan–Sep 2026) while EFID data is full-year (Jan–Dec 2025). ABUK's full-year 2026 report is not yet in the evidence.
2. EFID's EPS is on a consolidated basis; ABUK's is from a 9-month results release. Consolidation scopes may differ.
3. EPS is a per-share metric; it does not account for differences in share count, market capitalisation, sector, dividend policy, or valuation. ABUK trades at 76.21 EGP and EFID at 20.40 EGP, so the price-to-EPS multiples are very different.
4. Both companies show roughly 2× YoY EPS growth, but from very different absolute bases. A 5-year comparison would benefit from seeing ABUK's FY-2026 annual report and at least one more year of EFID results.

**Why keep_cash?**
Your question was an informational comparison, not a request to open a position. You currently hold no shares, and the evidence does not give me a verified full-year ABUK figure or a valuation framework (P/E, dividend yield, sector risk) sufficient to recommend buying either stock at this time. I would want ABUK's FY-2026 annual results and a clearer picture of each company's balance-sheet risk before suggesting a trade. Your 35,000 EGP remains available when you are ready to act.

# ABUK Full-Year 2026 EPS Estimate vs. EFID FY2025 EPS

## 1. What the evidence gives us

| Metric | Value | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| ABUK 9M-2026 basic EPS | **8.74 EGP** | [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-31] | Verified |
| ABUK 9M-2025 basic EPS | **4.28 EGP** | [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-32] | Verified |
| ABUK Q3-2025 basic EPS | **1.23 EGP** | [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-35] | Verified |
| ABUK Q3-2026 basic EPS | "199" | [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-34] | **AMBIGUOUS** – OCR dropped a decimal comma; could be 1.99, 19.9, or 199. **Not used in any calculation below.** |
| ABUK 9M YoY change | "%104" | [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-33] | **AMBIGUOUS** – formatting unclear. **Not used.** |
| ABUK Q3 YoY change | "662" | [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-36] | **AMBIGUOUS** – same OCR issue. **Not used.** |
| EFID FY2025 basic & diluted EPS | **2.18 EGP** | [EFID-EFID_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_signed_en-p6-38] | Verified |
| EFID FY2024 basic & diluted EPS | **1.09 EGP** | [EFID-EFID_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_signed_en-p6-39] | Verified |

> **Data-quality note on units:** The page-level unit line for the ABUK table reads "مليون جنيه" (million EGP), but the EPS row label itself explicitly states "جنيه" (EGP). The per-share figures are therefore in **whole EGP per share**, not millions. The "million EGP" unit applies to the other (total) rows on that page.

## 2. Estimating ABUK full-year 2026 EPS

**What I can do:**
- 9M-2026 EPS is confirmed at **8.74 EGP** [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-31].
- Full-year 2026 EPS = 9M-2026 + Q4-2026.

**What I cannot do with the evidence provided:**
- I have **no Q4-2026 figure** and **no FY-2025 figure** for ABUK, so I cannot derive a Q4 seasonal run-rate.
- The Q3-2026 figure is **AMBIGUOUS** [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-34], so I cannot back out H1-2026 or validate the 9M total against a quarterly build-up.
- The YoY change percentages are also **AMBIGUOUS** [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-33, p2-36], so I cannot cross-check the 9M growth rate.

**Reasonable bound (not a point estimate):**
- If Q4-2026 EPS is zero (a floor assumption), FY-2026 EPS = **8.74 EGP**.
- If Q4-2026 mirrors the Q3-2025 seasonal level of 1.23 EGP [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-35] (a very conservative proxy, since 2026 is running well ahead of 2025), FY-2026 EPS ≈ 8.74 + 1.23 = **≈ 9.97 EGP**.
- A more realistic Q4, given the 9M is already 104 % above the prior-year 9M, would likely push FY-2026 EPS into the **10–12 EGP** range, but I have no verified Q4 or FY-2025 data to anchor that.

**Bottom line for the estimate:** ABUK's FY-2026 EPS is **at least 8.74 EGP** and most plausibly in the **9–12 EGP** band. I flag this as a **range, not a point estimate**, because the Q4 component is not in the evidence.

## 3. Head-to-head: ABUK FY-2026 vs. EFID FY-2025

| | ABUK (est. FY-2026) | EFID (FY-2025) |
|---|---|---|
| EPS | ≥ 8.74 EGP (floor); ≈ 10–12 EGP (plausible) | **2.18 EGP** [EFID-EFID_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_signed_en-p6-38] |
| YoY growth context | 9M-2026 (8.74) vs 9M-2025 (4.28) → roughly 2× [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-31, p2-32] | FY-2025 (2.18) vs FY-2024 (1.09) → roughly 2× [EFID-EFID_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_signed_en-p6-38, p6-39] |

**Does ABUK beat EFID?**
Yes, on the evidence available. Even the **9-month** ABUK EPS of 8.74 EGP [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-31] is **four times** EFID's **full-year** 2025 EPS of 2.18 EGP [EFID-EFID_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_signed_en-p6-38]. For ABUK's full-year 2026 EPS to fall below 2.18 EGP, Q4-2026 would need to be a loss of more than 6.56 EGP per share – an outcome with no support in the provided data.

## 4. Caveats and data-quality flags

1. **ABUK Q3-2026 EPS is AMBIGUOUS** [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-34]. The printed "199" is almost certainly "1.99" (a dropped decimal comma), but I have **not** used it in any calculation.
2. **ABUK YoY change percentages are AMBIGUOUS** [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-33, p2-36]. I relied on the absolute EPS figures instead.
3. **No FY-2025 or Q4-2026 ABUK data** is in the evidence, so the full-year figure is a bounded estimate, not a verified number.
4. **EFID figures are consolidated** (per the row label "Basic and Diluted earnings per share (consolidated)"), while ABUK's are from a 9-month results release. The two companies may use different consolidation scopes; a like-for-like comparison would ideally use the same basis.
5. **Different reporting periods:** ABUK data is 9-month (Jan–Sep 2026); EFID data is full-year (Jan–Dec 2025). The comparison is therefore "ABUK 9M-2026 (and estimated FY-2026)" vs. "EFID FY-2025," not a same-period comparison.
6. **Scale / share-count differences:** ABUK trades at 76.21 EGP and EFID at 20.40 EGP. The EPS comparison is on a per-share basis and does not account for differences in share count, market cap, or sector.

## 5. Summary for the investor's 5-year, medium-risk comparison

- ABUK's earnings momentum in 2026 is strong: 9M EPS of 8.74 EGP vs. 4.28 EGP a year earlier [ABUK-ABUK_9M2026_results-p2-31, p2-32].
- EFID also doubled its EPS from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP year-on-year [EFID-EFID_FY2025_EAS_consolidated_signed_en-p6-39, p6-38], but from a much lower absolute base.
- On a pure EPS level, **ABUK's 2026 run-rate already exceeds EFID's entire 2025 EPS by a wide margin**, and the gap is likely to widen over the 5-year horizon if the 2026 growth trajectory persists.
- The main analytical gap is the **missing Q4-2026 / FY-2025 ABUK data** and the **AMBIGUOUS Q3-2026 figure**, which prevent a precise full-year number. I would want the ABUK FY-2026 annual report (or at least the Q4-2026 results) before treating the full-year EPS as a confirmed figure.

*No investment action is recommended here; the above is an evidence-based comparison only.*

## Estimating ABUK Full-Year 2026 EPS vs. EFID FY2025 EPS

### The arithmetic

| Item | Source | Value |
|---|---|---|
| ABUK basic EPS, 9 months ended 30 Sep 2026 | ABUK 9M-2026 results, p.2 (verified) | **8.74 EGP** |
| ABUK basic EPS, 9 months ended 30 Sep 2025 | same table (verified) | 4.28 EGP |
| EFID basic & diluted EPS, FY ended 31 Dec 2025 | EFID FY-2025 EAS, p.6 (verified) | **2.18 EGP** |

A straight annualisation of the 9-month figure:

$$\text{ABUK FY-2026e EPS} \approx 8.74 \times \frac{12}{9} \approx 11.65 \text{ EGP}$$

> **Caveat:** The Q3-2026 per-share cell in the same table prints as "١٩٩" with an OCR flag (a dropped decimal comma is suspected, i.e. likely 1.99 EGP). Because that figure is not verified, I cannot isolate Q4 and check whether the last quarter is seasonally heavier or lighter. The 11.65 EGP number is therefore a **pro-rata estimate only**, not a forecast.

### Head-to-head

| | ABUK FY-2026e | EFID FY-2025 |
|---|---|---|
| EPS | ≈ 11.65 EGP | 2.18 EGP |
| Ratio | **≈ 5.3×** | 1× |

On this simple EPS comparison, Abu Qir's estimated full-year 2026 earnings per share would be roughly **five times** Edita's 2025 figure. (This is an earnings-per-share comparison only; it does not account for share count, sector, dividend policy, or valuation.)

---

## Suitability snapshot (what the portfolio allows)

| Factor | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Horizon** | 5 years – comfortably long enough for an equity position in either exporter. |
| **Liquidity needs** | Emergency fund is held separately, so the 35,000 EGP in the portfolio is not earmarked for short-term bills. |
| **Loss willingness / capacity** | Both rated *medium*. A single-stock or two-stock equity sleeve is workable, but a large single-position bet (e.g. >70 % of the 35 k) would push past "medium" risk. |
| **Current concentration** | No holdings – the portfolio is 100 % cash, so there is no existing concentration to dilute. |
| **What can be sold** | Nothing (no securities held). |
| **Free cash** | **35,000 EGP** is fully available. |
| **Share counts at cutoff prices** | ABUK @ 76.21 EGP → ≈ 459 shares; EFID @ 20.40 EGP → ≈ 1,715 shares. |

Given medium loss tolerance, a reasonable commitment would leave a cash buffer (e.g. 20-30 % uninvested) and, if both names are considered, split the equity sleeve so neither single stock dominates. The 5-year horizon and separate emergency fund mean the investor is not forced to liquidate on a drawdown, which is the main thing that would otherwise constrain a medium-risk mandate.

*I have not selected a position or recommended a trade; the figures above are for the team's comparison exercise only.*
